newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Help Russian accused of treason, EU assembly asked.
newsitem.headline: Help Russian accused of treason, EU assembly asked.

text.p: A Norwegian environmental organisation urged the European Parliament on Wednesday to plead with Moscow to release Alexander Nikitin, a retired Russian navy nuclear safety inspector accused of leaking state secrets.
"We asked them in all their contacts with the Russians to say 'set Nikitin free'," Frederic Hauge, the director of the Bellona Foundation, told a news conference.
Bellona is campaigning to end nuclear contamination in north west Russia.

Nikitin was accused of treason in February by the Fedderal Security Service (FSB), the successor to the Soviet-era KGB, after publishing in a Bellona report information on radioactive contamination which the FSB said he had obtained illegally.
Hauge was speaking after he and Nikitin's lawyer Yuri Smidt met the European Parliament's delegation on Russia.
Smidt told the news conference the FSB's allegations were false since all the data used in the report was openly and legally available.
Hauge said the case set a dangerous precedent, both in human rights and environmental terms.
By declaring the information in the report illegal, the FSB risked putting the West off funding costly projects to prevent nuclear accidents in Russia.
The European Union, the U.S. and Norway are considering financing such a project.
"If this kind of uncertainty is... around environmental work, (Western governments and industries) will refuse to go in and work with the Russians," Hauge said.
Constantanze Krehl, the head of the EU assembly's delegation on Russia, said they would to raise the Nikitin case with the Russian parliament in December.
"We have to see he has all he needs for the trial...and has a quick trial," the German Euro-MP told Reuters.
